title: The pilgrim
hookLine: a wanderer hears one verse in church and sets out across Russia to learn what it means

cards: A man stands in a Russian church, listening to the reading. One line from a letter of Paul catches him and won't let go. In the King James wording it's three words: "Pray without ceasing."

How can anyone pray without stopping? People have to eat, sleep, work, talk. With a knapsack, some dried bread and a Bible, he starts walking, from church to church, from preacher to preacher, asking the same question.
Plenty of them explain why prayer matters. Nobody tells him how.

teach.b: The Way of a Pilgrim is a Russian book, written as one man's account of his own wandering. The pilgrim never gives his name. First, the question.
Paul's line in First Thessalonians sounds like a slogan. The pilgrim takes it literally, and the book takes his question seriously: if it's in the Bible, there must be a way. Second, the teacher.

teach.h: THE ELDER AND THE PRAYER ROPE.
teach.b: After a long search he meets an elder, a starets, who finally answers him: the way to pray without ceasing is the Jesus Prayer, said over and over.
He hands the pilgrim the Philokalia to read, and gives him a daily number of prayers to say on a prayer rope. Then he doubles it. Then doubles it again.
At first, the pilgrim tells us, it's work. Then it gets easier. Then the prayer seems to keep going on its own, under everything, while he walks, while he talks, even while he's half asleep.

He describes warmth in his heart and a new tenderness toward everyone he meets. Fourth, the road. The book is full of the people he runs into: thieves, a family who takes him in, travelers with stories of their own.
The prayer doesn't pull him away from the world.

teach.h: IT WALKS HIM INTO THE WORLD.
teach.b: It walks him into it. Some Orthodox readers come to the Jesus Prayer through this book, and the pilgrim keeps pointing back to his elder and the Philokalia. It's a picture of taking one line completely seriously.

how: Orthodox Christians read The Way of a Pilgrim as an introduction to the Jesus Prayer, and some take up the prayer with a prayer rope through the day, ideally under the guidance of a spiritual father or mother.

o: the unnamed wanderer who learned to pray without ceasing
an apostle who carried Paul's letters to the churches
a monk who walked to Jerusalem barefoot every year

p: the line he heard in church
the book the elder hands him

games.q: you're the pilgrim. every sermon explains why prayer matters, and nobody tells you how to pray without ceasing. what do you do?
o: decide the verse can't really mean it.
keep walking and asking until someone shows you.
make up a method of your own.
games.why: he keeps walking and asking until he meets an elder, a starets, who teaches him the Jesus Prayer.

practice: Choose one line or word to carry: if you pray, a line you already know from your own tradition, maybe yesterday's Jesus Prayer if you're a Christian; if you don't, a single plain word you'd like to live in, such as patience or here.
Say it silently, again and again, at whatever pace comes naturally. When you drift, come back to it without scolding; let it grow familiar.

wordCard.voice: The pilgrim. The unnamed wanderer of The Way of a Pilgrim, who walked across Russia asking how to pray without ceasing and learned the Jesus Prayer. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: without ceasing. Under everything, like the pilgrim's prayer on the road. See you tomorrow.
